test_title: PYST 5: SSC Stenographer - English (Held on: 15 Nov 2021 Shift 1 )
subject: english
question:
**Select the correct direct narration of the given sentence.**

I told my parents that I would miss them when I was away. I also requested them to take good care of themselves in my absence.

options.text: I said to my parents, "You will be missed when you are away. You should take good care of yourselves in my absence."
I said to my parents, "I'll have missed you when you are away. Please take good care of yourselves in my absence."
I said to my parents, "I had missed you when I'm away. You have to take good care of yourselves in my absence."
I said to my parents, "I'll miss you when I'm away. Please take good care of yourselves in my absence."

solution:
The correct answer is: **I said to my parents, "I'll miss you when I'm away. Please take good care of yourselves in my absence."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is an indirect speech and we need to convert it into direct speech.
 
• When we change an indirect speech to a direct speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• The reported verb 'requested' changes to 'said to' in the reporting speech part.
 
• To express the request phrase, "Please" is used in the indirect part and it changes to '**to**' in the direct speech. (Express request)
 
• The preposition 'to' is replaced with inverted commas ("...") to show the direct speech part.
 
• A comma (,) is added after the direct speech part.
 
• The first word of the direct speech is in capital letter.
 
• The past form of be verb 'was' changes to present form 'am' in the direct speech.
 
• The modal '**would**' changes to '**will**' in the direct speech.
 
• We use '**also**' in the indirect speech when there is more than one clause is given.
 
 

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

Hence, direct speech is - *I said to my parents, "I'll miss you when I'm away. Please take good care of yourselves in my absence."*
